rich_summary: Arjuna journeys north toward the Himalayas seeking divine weapons, driven by his resolve to avenge the wrongs done to his brothers. Moving with supernatural speed through mountains inhabited by ascetics, he reaches Indrakila where a radiant ascetic halts him and questions why a warrior bears weapons in a realm of peace. The ascetic reveals himself as Indra (Sakra) and offers Arjuna a boon, even suggesting heavenly bliss instead of warfare. Arjuna refuses comfort or paradise, insisting that honor demands he defeat his enemies before enjoying any reward. Impressed by this resolve, Indra tells him he must first win the favor of Shiva to obtain celestial weapons. The narrative then frames the coming episode: Arjuna’s intense austerities and the extraordinary encounter with Shiva that will test and transform him.

highlight_spans.why: Arjuna’s purposeful journey toward Indra begins, establishing the quest for divine weapons and the epic scale of his travel.
At Indrakila a mysterious voice commands Arjuna to stop, initiating the pivotal encounter with the disguised deity.
The ascetic argues that weapons have no place in a realm of peaceful sages, highlighting the tension between warrior duty and ascetic renunciation.
Arjuna passionately rejects heavenly bliss, declaring he cannot accept joy while his brothers remain wronged and unavenged.
Indra reveals the true path: Arjuna must first behold and win the favor of Shiva to receive celestial weapons.

top_scenes.scene_text: Arjuna standing armed on the heights of Indrakila as a radiant ascetic beneath a tree halts him with a divine command.
Indra revealing his true divine form before Arjuna after appearing as a humble ascetic in the Himalayan wilderness.
Arjuna alone in the vast Himalayan forest beginning severe austerities amid rivers, birds, and towering mountains.
